newsitem.title: MONACO: TENNIS-RIOS ENDS SPANISH DOMINANCE ON CLAY.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-RIOS ENDS SPANISH DOMINANCE ON CLAY.

text.p: Chile's Marcelo Rios ended Spanish dominance on clay so far this season when he beat Alex Corretja in straight sets to win the Monte Carlo Open on Sunday.
The 21-year Chilean, seeded seventh, crushed the Spaniard 6-4 6-3 6-3 in a one-sided match for the most impressive victory of his career.
Rios has won four previous ATP Tour events but none as prestigious as this $2.3 million clay court tournament.
"I played well and had a great time in Monte Carlo all week -- even if I lost some money at the casino," he said.
As well as defeating Corretja, winner in Estoril two weeks ago, Rios had earlier disposed of Spain's Albert Costa, winner of the European season's second clay court tournament in Barcelona last week.

A semifinalist here last year, Rios confirmed he would again be one of the players to watch on the slow surface after a lacklustre hard-court season in which he reached only one final, in Marseille two months ago.

A versatile player, as comfortable at the baseline as at the net, the Chilean mastered the windy conditions far better than Corretja, seeded 12th, who looked tired and made an unusual amount of unforced errors.
The most strongly contested game of the match was the last in which Corretja, refusing to bow, saved four match points.
The third match point saw the Spaniard return two smashes before forcing Rios to push a volley into the net. But Corretja had left his fightback far too late.
He had also saved two set points in the first set before losing 6-4 in 43 minutes and Rios comfortably won a dull second set in which the wind at times made rallies almost impossible.

Corretja fought harder at the beginning of the third set to salvage some pride but Rios, hitting punishing forehands on the important points was far too solid and he once more broke the 23-year-old for a 3-1 lead.
His task had been made easier by the early defeat of top seeds Pete Sampras, Thomas Muster and Yevgeny Kafelnikov, but Rios will now fancy his chances in next month's French Open.
